narrative_purpose: A microscopic border scene replaces the simplistic 'alien germ equals instant plague' trope with the sequence of ecological and molecular gates any cross-biosphere pathogen would need to cross.
subject: A close cutaway of blue living skin forming a broad vertical boundary at center. On the left, a sparse cluster of Earth-like microbial rods and spheres approaches through air and moisture; most fail to attach and drift away. At one small contact point a hooked cell reaches a membrane receptor but does not fit. On the right, native Pandoran surface microbes already occupy dense protective films and niches. Beneath the skin, quiet immune-like cells wait in tissue, separated from the outside by intact layers.
scene: Abstract but organic microscopic space at the interface between two biospheres, with a single continuous skin barrier and dark clean surroundings.
camera: Straight-on high-magnification cutaway, external microbes left, barrier center, resident community and tissue defences right and below.
light: Cyan rim on the skin barrier, teal glow for resident organisms, sparse amber for rejected outsiders, restrained magenta at the mismatched receptor contact.
palette: Deep indigo ground, blue-cyan tissue, living teal residents, sparse amber outsiders and one magenta incompatibility accent.
style: Painterly microscopic naturalist diagram, tactile membranes and cells, elegant rather than vector-clean.
detail_level: Crisp at the skin layers, mismatched receptor, resident film and waiting immune cells; generous deep indigo negative space.
composition: A strong central barrier dividing the frame, multiple successive filtering steps readable from left to right in space, clear negative space near each barrier.
consistency_notes: Communicate barriers and incompatibility spatially. Avoid implying guaranteed safety or guaranteed infection; the image represents filters, not a verdict.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no labels, no arrows, no infographic chrome, no gore, no giant horror microbes, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
